worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=a$ and $n=9$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+a)}^{9} & =1+9\cdot a+\frac{9(9-1)}{2!}\cdot {a}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+9a+\frac{9\cdot 8}{2}\cdot {a}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+9a+36{a}^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
